report.summary: An infrastructure node pool patch at 13:36:00 UTC updated node pool np-3 and changed time synchronization from chrony to systemd-timesyncd, causing a +99s clock offset on node np-3-a1. This clock skew caused auth-service pods running on that node to reject incoming JWTs due to 'token issued in the future (iat skew)' starting at 13:40:00 UTC, leading to user login failures.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Node image update time-sync configuration shift causes clock skew and JWT iat validation failure

supporting.note: Infrastructure update changing time sync method occurred at 13:36:00 UTC, four minutes prior to the incident onset.
Kubernetes node log explicitly shows clock offset +99s on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39:27.
auth-service pod on node np-3-a1 explicitly logged JWT validation failure due to iat skew starting at 13:40:09 UTC.
auth-service error rate spiked sharply from 0.28% to over 30% starting at 13:40:00 UTC.
mobile-bff received 401 responses from auth-service starting at 13:40:18 UTC.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Delayed bug in auth-service session refresh release triggered by standard time validation

supporting.note: auth-service was deployed to version v7.2.0 two days prior to the incident.
auth-service error rate increased dramatically during the incident.

contradicting.note: The incident onset correlates precisely with the time-sync infrastructure change at 13:36:00 UTC rather than the deployment time two days prior.

facts.text: auth-service error rate spiked from baseline 0.28% to 32.36% at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00.
mobile-bff error rate spiked from baseline 0.32% to 5.93% at 2026-10-16T13:40:00+00:00.
auth-service began logging JWT validation errors due to iat skew starting at 2026-10-16T13:40:09+00:00.
mobile-bff began logging 401 responses from auth-service for POST /v1/session starting at 2026-10-16T13:40:18+00:00.
An infrastructure change on kubernetes node pool np-3 (new node image 2026.10.3, time sync: chrony -> systemd-timesyncd) occurred at 2026-10-16T13:36:00+00:00.
Kubernetes logs began showing clock synchronization warnings on node np-3-a1 starting at 13:39:27, showing a clock offset of +99s.

assumptions: The change from chrony to systemd-timesyncd caused an abrupt clock step or drift on node np-3-a1 rather than smooth synchronization.

timeline.event: auth-service was deployed to version v7.2.0
Infrastructure change on kubernetes node pool np-3 changing time sync from chrony to systemd-timesyncd
Kubernetes node np-3-a1 logs clock offset +99s exceeding threshold
auth-service and mobile-bff error rates spike
auth-service logs JWT validation failure due to iat skew on node np-3-a1
mobile-bff logs 401 response from upstream auth-service

recommended_actions.action: Resync or reboot node np-3-a1 to correct the systemd-timesyncd clock drift immediately.
recommended_actions.rationale: Node np-3-a1 has a +99s clock offset causing active JWT validation failures.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back or re-configure time-sync settings on node pool np-3 from systemd-timesyncd back to chrony if desynchronization persists.
recommended_actions.rationale: The clock drift was introduced directly following the node image update and time-sync configuration change.

recommended_actions.action: Implement strict pre-release validation for node pool images concerning time synchronization accuracy.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents future infrastructure updates from silently altering time-sync mechanisms and causing cluster-wide authentication failures.
